audit.why: Disk win rate is exactly 50.0% over 78 games — the smallest sample in the slice — and both layers agree the lane is a poke stalemate you resolve in teamfights. The chart tilts Kennen 4-2, which is a touch strong for a coin flip but is defensible given he owns the whole 2-5 stretch.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 section says Slicing Maelstrom 'costs a lot of energy and has a long cooldown', and neither half is accurate as written.
audit.why: Slicing Maelstrom costs 0 and is a flat 120 seconds at all three ranks. That combination is the actual spike shape: he never has to hold it back for resources, but once it is gone it is gone for two full minutes and does not shorten as he ranks it. Lightning Rush is 10/9/8/7/6s and Electrical Surge 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6s.
audit.corrected: Replaced with 'costs him no energy but is a flat 120 seconds at every rank' in mid, spikes[1] and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The stun is attributed to a two-hit chain in two fields — 'stack a W passive mark with a follow-up auto or Q', 'a Q into auto procs the stun'. Mark of the Storm needs three marks, not two. The entry also calls the stun a 'W passive'; the stun lives on his actual passive.
audit.why: Riot text: Mark of the Storm (P) — 'Kennen stuns enemies he hits 3 times with his abilities.' Electrical Surge (W) 'passively deals extra damage and adds a Mark of the Storm to his target every few attacks, and he can activate this ability to damage and add another Mark to targets who are already marked.' Counting to two instead of three means stepping up on the exact beat the stun lands.
audit.corrected: Stated the three-mark requirement and the real chain: Q, a marked auto off Electrical Surge, then the W activation.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pillar of Ice is credited with a knockup ('walk in to poke without eating a knockup') and with self-displacement ('Pillar-displace yourself out of the AOE'). Riot's description supports neither. Chomp is also credited with an AS steal in early, whys[0] and spikes[3].
audit.why: Riot text: Pillar of Ice 'creates an ice pillar at target location, becoming impassable terrain and slowing all nearby enemy units' — terrain and a slow, no displacement of anyone including yourself. Chomp saps Attack Damage. Telling a player he can Pillar himself out of Slicing Maelstrom is advice that will get him killed at level 6.
audit.corrected: Pillar reframed as terrain plus slow, self-displacement removed in favour of simply stepping clear of the storm, and the AS claims swapped for the AD drain and the Chomp slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Kennen's damage rides attack speed, so the entry gives no reason to prefer anything over flat armour.
audit.why: Electrical Surge applies on-hit as he attacks, which means his output scales with attack speed and an armour-only response misreads the trade.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lightning Rush is called 'his escape' in the full layer with no mention that it passes through units.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Kennen morphs into a lightning form, enabling him to pass through units and apply a Mark of the Storm.' Body-blocking him with the wave, and ganks that rely on the minion line holding him, both fail.
audit.corrected: Added the pass-through-units clause and the 10s rank-1 cooldown to the cooldown block.

edits.before: At level 1 you both probe the wave — Kennen's Q has no kill threat yet and you can trade a Q Chomp if he steps to his own minions, stealing a chunk of his AS and healing off any dying minion through King's Tribute; it is nearly even if you respect his range. The moment he hits level 2 and can stack a W passive mark with a follow-up auto or Q, the lane tilts his way: he can poke you to half HP before you are close enough to drop Frozen Domain. Pre-place W not when you want to fight but a full step BEFORE you intend to walk up — Kennen won't enter a zone he can see glowing, but it forces him to back off lane position and spend energy to reposition. At level 3 his Q-auto-W stun rotation is live; do NOT approach in a straight line, juke to bait the Q, then close.
edits.after: At level 1 you both probe the wave — Thundering Shuriken has no kill threat yet and you can trade a Chomp if he steps to his own minions, sapping his AD and healing off any dying minion through King's Tribute; it is nearly even if you respect his range. The moment he hits level 2 the lane tilts his way: Mark of the Storm stuns on the third mark, not the second, so the real chain is Q, then a marked auto off Electrical Surge, then the W activation. Pre-place W a full step BEFORE you intend to walk up, not when you want to fight — Kennen won't enter a zone he can see glowing, so it costs him lane position and energy to reposition. At level 3 do NOT approach in a straight line; juke to bait the Q, then close.

edits.before: You can trade a Q Chomp into his level-1 auto and steal his AS while healing off dying minions, but Kennen's 525 auto range means he never has to stand next to you — it is genuinely even if both players play carefully.
edits.after: You can trade a Q Chomp into his level-1 auto and sap his AD while healing off dying minions, but Kennen's ranged auto means he never has to stand next to you — it is genuinely even if both players play carefully.

edits.before: Kennen's W passive mark activates the moment he hits level 2: a Q into auto procs the stun and you absorb it mid-approach with no Frozen Domain up yet — he controls the tempo from here.
edits.after: Electrical Surge comes online at level 2, but Mark of the Storm needs three marks: Q, a marked auto, then the W activation. You absorb that chain mid-approach with no Frozen Domain up yet.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are his strongest sustained poke window — you have Chomp and Pillar but no ultimate, and every Q-poke chips you faster than King's Tribute and W healing offset the damage unless you stay on your ice island constantly. Use Pillar of Ice not as an engage tool but as a zoning deterrent: drop it at the edge of your Frozen Domain so Kennen cannot walk in to poke without eating a knockup. At level 6 his R is genuinely scary — he can Flash-R onto you, stun you for the entire channel, and drain most of your HP before Subjugate's first tick lands. You are not defenceless: his R costs a lot of energy and has a long cooldown, so if you bait it by walking up and then Pillar-displace yourself out of the AOE, you can immediately Subjugate and Frozen Domain him while he has no defensive tool left. That is your only clean level-6 all-in — do not force it otherwise.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his strongest sustained poke window — you have Chomp and Pillar but no ultimate, and every Q chips you faster than King's Tribute and W healing offset it unless you stay on your ice island. Use Pillar of Ice as a zoning deterrent, not an engage tool: it is impassable terrain that slows everything near it, so at the edge of Frozen Domain it forces Kennen the long way round to poke. At level 6 Slicing Maelstrom is genuinely scary — Flash-R onto you, marks chaining through the whole channel, most of your HP gone before Subjugate's first tick. You are not defenceless: R costs him no energy but it is a flat 120 seconds at every rank, so bait it by walking up, step clear of the storm, then Subjugate and Frozen Domain a Kennen with no ultimate left. That is your only clean level-6 all-in.

edits.before: Once you have Iceborn Gauntlet and can hit him with the Spellblade-enhanced Chomp after a Pillar knockup, your burst window closes enough to survive his poke and threaten a kill; the lane stabilises into farm for both sides, which is reflected in the 48.68% even split. Teamfights are where you reclaim the game — Subjugate on their front-line tank (not Kennen himself) drains armour and MR directly onto you, and dropping Pillar at a choke while you stand in Frozen Domain makes you nearly unkillable. Against a tanky enemy comp your Subjugate pays off massively; even a relatively even laning phase means you come out of the mid-game with enough stats to anchor fights and let your carries clean up behind the pillar wall.

notes: Disk 50.0% / 78 games; packet says 48.68% / 76, and the existing late text quoted 48.68% in prose, which no longer matched the disk table it renders next to — I changed the prose to 50% for internal consistency, but if the packet is the newer source then the WR table is what needs updating instead and that is outside my write scope. Left alone and unverified: the claim that Kennen's auto range is 525. The kit files do not carry attack ranges, and I believe 525 is wrong, so I removed the number rather than substitute a guess.
